nodes.summary: In a multigraph $G$, a vertex $v$ is adjacent to a vertex $w$ if and only if $w$ is adjacent to $v$.
nodes.title: Symmetry of adjacency in a multigraph

nodes.summary: Two vertices $v$ and $w$ of a multigraph $G$ are adjacent when the edge multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive.
nodes.title: Adjacency in a multigraph

nodes.summary: In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano, for vertices $v$ and $w$, $(v, w)$ is an ascending edge if and only if $(w, v)$ is a descending edge.
nodes.title: Reversing an ascending edge gives a descending edge

nodes.summary: In a multigraph $G$, every vertex $v$ is connected to $v$.
nodes.title: Every vertex is connected to itself

nodes.summary: Two vertices $v$ and $w$ of a multigraph $G$ are connected when they are related by the reflexive-transitive closure of adjacency, that is, when there is a finite sequence of vertices $v = u_0, u_1, \dots, u_k = w$ with $k \ge 0$ and $u_i$ adjacent to $u_{i+1}$ for each $i < k$.
nodes.title: Connectivity of vertices in a multigraph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a multigraph on a finite vertex set $V$, let $v \in V$ and let $P$ be a decidable predicate on $V$. Then the degree of $v$ equals the degree of $v$ restricted to $P$ plus the degree of $v$ restricted to $\neg P$.
nodes.title: Degree splits over a predicate and its complement

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a multigraph on a finite vertex set $V$, let $v \in V$ and let $P$ and $Q$ be decidable predicates on $V$. If $P(w) \iff Q(w)$ for every vertex $w$ whose edge multiplicity with $v$ is positive, then the degree of $v$ restricted to $P$ equals the degree of $v$ restricted to $Q$.
nodes.title: Restricted degree depends only on the neighbours

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a multigraph on a finite vertex set $V$ with edge multiplicity $m$, let $v \in V$ and let $P$ be a decidable predicate on $V$. The degree of $v$ restricted to $P$ is $\sum_{w \in V,\, P(w)} m(v, w)$.
nodes.title: Degree restricted to a predicate

nodes.summary: For a multigraph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$ with edge multiplicity $m$, the degree of a vertex $v$ is $\sum_{w \in V} m(v, w)$. A loop at $v$ contributes its multiplicity once, matching the outgoing-isogeny convention.
nodes.title: Degree of a vertex in a multigraph

nodes.summary: In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano, for vertices $v$ and $w$, $(v, w)$ is a descending edge if and only if $(w, v)$ is an ascending edge.
nodes.title: Reversing a descending edge gives an ascending edge

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be an $\ell$-isogeny volcano, with levels numbered from $0$ at the surface, and let $v, w$ be vertices of $C$ whose edge multiplicity is positive. Then $(v, w)$ is a horizontal edge (both $v$ and $w$ have level $0$), a descending edge (the level of $w$ is the level of $v$ plus one) or an ascending edge (the level of $v$ is the level of $w$ plus one).
nodes.title: Every edge of an isogeny volcano is horizontal, descending or ascending

nodes.summary: In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$, the pair $(v, w)$ of vertices is an ascending edge when the edge multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive and $w$ lies one level above $v$, that is, the level of $w$ plus one equals the level of $v$ (level $0$ being the surface).
nodes.title: Ascending edge

nodes.summary: A multigraph $G$ is connected when every two vertices $v$ and $w$ of $G$ are joined by a walk, that is, $w$ is reachable from $v$ by a finite (possibly empty) sequence of steps along edges of positive multiplicity.
nodes.title: Connected multigraph

nodes.summary: In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$, the pair $(v, w)$ of vertices is a descending edge when the edge multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive and $w$ lies one level below $v$, that is, the level of $v$ plus one equals the level of $w$ (level $0$ being the surface).
nodes.title: Descending edge

nodes.summary: A vertex $v$ of an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$ lies on the floor of $C$ if and only if the level of $v$, as a natural number, equals the depth of $C$.
nodes.title: Floor vertices are those whose level equals the depth

nodes.summary: A vertex $v$ of an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$ of depth $d$ lies on the floor of $C$ when its level is $d$, the last of the levels $0, 1, \dots, d$.
nodes.title: Floor of a volcano

nodes.summary: In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$, the pair $(v, w)$ of vertices is a horizontal edge when the edge multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive and both $v$ and $w$ lie on the surface, that is, both have level $0$.
nodes.title: Horizontal edge

nodes.summary: A vertex $v$ of an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$ lies on the surface of $C$ if and only if the level of $v$, as a natural number, is $0$.
nodes.title: Surface vertices are those of level zero

nodes.summary: A vertex $v$ of an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$ lies on the surface of $C$ when its level is $0$.
nodes.title: Surface of a volcano

nodes.summary: In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$, the pair $(v, w)$ of vertices is a vertical edge when it is a descending edge or an ascending edge, that is, when the edge multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive and the levels of $v$ and $w$ differ by exactly one.
nodes.title: Vertical edge

nodes.summary: Let $\ell$ be a prime. An $\ell$-isogeny volcano consists of a finite vertex set $V$, a multigraph on $V$ with edge multiplicities $m(v, w)$, a depth $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a surjective level map $\mathrm{lev} : V \to \{0, 1, \dots, d\}$ and a surface degree $s \in \mathbb{N}$ with $s \le 2$, subject to the following conditions, where the surface is the set of vertices of level $0$. Every surface vertex $v$ satisfies…
nodes.title: Isogeny volcano

nodes.summary: A multigraph on a vertex set $V$ is given by an edge multiplicity function $m$ that assigns to every two vertices $v, w \in V$ a natural number $m(v, w)$ and is symmetric: $m(v, w) = m(w, v)$ for all $v, w \in V$. Loops are permitted: $m(v, v)$ may be positive.
nodes.title: Multigraph

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be an $\ell$-isogeny volcano with edge multiplicities $m$ and surface degree $s$. For every surface vertex $v$ of $C$, that is, every vertex of level $0$, the sum of $m(v, w)$ over all surface vertices $w$ of $C$ equals $s$.
nodes.title: Surface regularity of an isogeny volcano

nodes.summary: The depth of an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$ is the natural number $d$ recorded in $C$: the levels of the vertices of $C$ are exactly $0, 1, \dots, d$, with level $0$ the surface and level $d$ the floor.
nodes.title: Depth of an isogeny volcano

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
